scenario: Forged replayed or misbound OIDC material is accepted as a Veer principal or for the wrong audience
existing_controls: OIDC short lifetime and token exclusion are accepted requirements but no runtime exists
mitigation: Validate issuer audience algorithm signature expiry skew JWKS rotation and replay behavior; separate human and workload flows; retain a negative token and redaction corpus
residual_risk: Identity-provider compromise or a valid stolen token remains usable until bounded expiry or revocation

scenario: A principal authorized in one workspace gains another workspace or administrator action through incomplete scope or role logic
existing_controls: Default deny stable identifiers and separate platform administration are accepted invariants
mitigation: Define a complete deterministic role and action matrix; require stable workspace and parent scope; prevent self escalation; enforce admission and execution checks
residual_risk: An authorized workspace administrator can still make harmful choices inside the owned workspace

scenario: A stale plan or queued operation executes after actor revocation policy change generation change or approval expiry
existing_controls: Plans are required to persist actor policy and generation context but execution is not implemented
mitigation: Bind plan and approval to actor policy generation connection capability quota cost and digest; reauthorize immediately before every provider effect
residual_risk: Revocation propagation and provider calls already in flight have a bounded race that must become explicit terminal state

scenario: ProviderConnection substitution or destination mutation turns Veer into a confused deputy for another workspace or environment
existing_controls: Adapters are required to receive scoped execution context rather than caller credentials
mitigation: Bind immutable connection ownership destination workspace environment actor policy generation and operation; verify current scope and recipient before brokering a session
residual_risk: A provider administrator can intentionally broaden or redirect a provider identity outside Veer's control

scenario: Provider or user credential material escapes through serialization plans state logs traces metrics errors fixtures crash output or support bundles
existing_controls: Secret references external storage and redaction are accepted requirements
mitigation: Use memory-only short sessions with no marshal or string surface; field allowlists and secret denylist; canary tests across every output; revoke and rotate independently
residual_risk: A compromised process can use a valid in-memory session until expiry revocation or lost ownership

scenario: The effective AWS role Kubernetes service account resource policy or cluster permission is broader than the declared workspace and environment
existing_controls: Dedicated short-lived identities are required but their effective policies are not implemented or qualified
mitigation: Use dedicated identities restrictive trust and resource policy session restrictions source identity bound K8s tokens least-privilege RBAC live identity verification and policy analysis
residual_risk: Veer cannot reduce an independently broad provider resource policy or provider administrator authority

scenario: A storage query migration role table owner or row-policy bypass reads or changes another workspace or removes tenant constraints
existing_controls: Stable workspace keys parameterized SQL and separated database roles are accepted design rules
mitigation: Require composite ownership constraints and scope-bearing query APIs; use non-owner NOBYPASSRLS runtime with forced RLS defense in depth; test every query and migration
residual_risk: Privileged migration backup and recovery roles necessarily cross workspace storage and remain high-impact trust anchors

scenario: Poisoned duplicated reordered or replayed queue work is treated as current execution authority
existing_controls: Queue payloads are bounded non-secret references and at-least-once delivery is explicit
mitigation: Use exact producer and consumer policies bounded schema authoritative state reload current authorization generation and digest checks fences idempotency bounded DLQ and audited redrive
residual_risk: An uncertain queue acknowledgement can duplicate delivery and must remain harmless rather than impossible

scenario: A stale worker continues provider or state mutation after visibility lease or database fence loss
existing_controls: StateStore requires monotonic fencing and commit-before-ack semantics
mitigation: Fence every external attempt and result commit; stop on lease-extension failure; use idempotency and ownership keys; exercise pause partition duplicate and replacement races
residual_risk: A provider call with an unknown outcome cannot be made exactly once and needs observation plus terminal operator-visible state

scenario: A malicious manifest webhook provider response or external state causes injection SSRF unsafe destination resource exhaustion secret reflection or mutation without ownership
existing_controls: External inputs are declared untrusted and adapters are required to be typed and narrow
mitigation: Use closed schemas byte depth and count limits verified endpoints parameterized operations safe errors ownership proofs fuzz seeds and mandatory fake-provider conformance
residual_risk: Provider behavior can remain inconsistent or unavailable even after malformed data is rejected

scenario: Required audit data is omitted altered deleted reordered or exported incompletely so privileged activity can be repudiated
existing_controls: Required audit events are accepted as atomic and immutable design invariants
mitigation: Define canonical event and sequence; insert atomically with state; use integrity chain and manifest immutable archive role separation gap detection scoped query and export verification
residual_risk: Simultaneous compromise of relational audit archive and both integrity key boundaries can defeat detection

scenario: Break-glass redrive migration repair or recovery bypasses ordinary policy without durable scope reason and accountability
existing_controls: Platform and workspace administration are required to be separate
mitigation: Require strong authentication separate roles exact action and scope reason time limit dry run approval when required immutable audit and no routine direct database edits
residual_risk: An authorized platform operator remains capable of high-impact actions during the approved elevation window

scenario: A migration or configuration change removes tenant constraints role separation audit atomicity redaction or safe endpoints
existing_controls: SQL-only immutable migrations typed configuration and role separation are selected design requirements
mitigation: Use checksummed ordered migrations dedicated migrator transactional default closed config schema schema manifest rollback tests and post-change invariant scans
residual_risk: A correctly authorized but harmful migration can still require restore and forward repair rather than automatic rollback

scenario: A deletion race false ownership stale external identifier or failed compensation deletes an unowned resource or conceals an orphan
existing_controls: Cancellation finalization ownership and orphan visibility are required but not implemented
mitigation: Bind ownership proof generation and fence to delete; use dependency-aware finalizers retry-safe delete compensation distinct from rollback orphan inventory quarantine and audit
residual_risk: Provider-side partial effects and unknown outcomes may require manual recovery and retained cost until reconciled

scenario: Backup or restore crosses workspace scope uses tampered or stale data or revives obsolete credentials and policy
existing_controls: Encrypted isolated restore integrity verification and authority revalidation are accepted recovery targets
mitigation: Use signed common checkpoint separate roles and keys immutable audit isolated restore complete ledger comparison new workload credentials policy revalidation and gated cutover
residual_risk: Compromise of both regional key boundaries or corruption older than retention remains outside the alpha recovery claim

scenario: A mutable dependency action tag registry input local release or stolen automation identity publishes attacker-controlled code
existing_controls: Bootstrap tools are pinned and checksum verified but release supply-chain controls are not implemented
mitigation: Require protected checks immutable actions and dependencies secret dependency static license container and IaC scans ephemeral least privilege reproducible release SBOM signature provenance and consumer verification
residual_risk: A protected signing or release identity remains a critical trust anchor whose compromise requires revocation and incident response

scenario: One workspace exhausts API queue database provider telemetry cardinality retained bytes or financial budget and starves others
existing_controls: ADR 0001 defines capacity SLO and cost ceilings as design gates
mitigation: Enforce body and request limits quotas fair scheduling bounded concurrency backoff provider-call budgets telemetry meters cardinality registry and workspace cost attribution
residual_risk: A provider outage or valid workload burst can still reduce freshness within the documented exclusion and budget boundaries

scenario: Personal configuration or operational values leak through logs traces metric labels errors status exports or support output
existing_controls: Redaction low-cardinality metrics and bounded retention are accepted requirements
mitigation: Apply the most restrictive data class before emission; allowlist fields; use opaque correlation and scoped export; enforce retention deletion canaries and cardinality tests
residual_risk: Authorized operators retain access to bounded operational and audit data required for support and incident response

scenario: Approval of one plan digest or policy state authorizes a changed plan stale capability drifted resource or self-approved broader effect
existing_controls: Plans are required to be immutable deterministic and bound to policy context
mitigation: Bind approval to canonical digest actor scope policy capability quota cost generation and expiry; prohibit unauthorized self approval; re-plan on drift; reauthorize execution
residual_risk: A legitimately authorized approver can approve harmful intent within their current scope

scenario: The provider destination or credential identity resolves to an unintended AWS account partition region or Kubernetes cluster
existing_controls: Capability discovery and destination verification are required before execution
mitigation: Verify TLS peer and configured endpoint; check AWS caller account partition region and role; check Kubernetes server CA cluster and namespace; bind exact connection; fail mismatches closed
residual_risk: Compromise of provider DNS PKI account administrator or cluster administrator remains outside ordinary tenant authority

scenario: Archive cleanup authority targets the active baseline or bypasses retention without valid recovery state
existing_controls: ADR 0001 defines separate sweeper validator and cleanup roles but none is implemented
mitigation: Require exact candidate or retired tag and prefix signed abort or promotion state short cleanup session active-baseline bucket-policy deny no retention or legal-hold mutation explicit bypass immutable audit and final empty-version proof
residual_risk: A correctly authorized cleanup permanently destroys its selected non-authoritative generation so target and state verification remain critical trust anchors
